result:
All checks pass. Summary of what was done:

**Bug 1 — rotate.sh** (`rotate.sh:100-108`): the old `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"`, which selects from the *keep*-th line of a list sorted oldest-first — so with exactly N archives it deleted one (the newest), and in general it deleted the newest archives instead of the oldest. Now `surplus()` emits the oldest `total-keep` lines (`head -n "$((total - keep))"`), and the early exit uses `-le` so nothing is deleted (and `head -n 0` never runs on BSD head) when `total <= keep`.

**Bug 2 — verify.sh** (`verify.sh:96-100,112`): `awk '{print $2}'` split the sidecar line on every space, truncating `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz` to `my` → "archive missing"/BAD. The line is now split with `read -r expected file <<< "$line"` (digest + full remainder), and the digest comparison is properly quoted.

**Refactor**: new `lib/common.sh` holds the shared option-parsing block (`--dest/--name/--keep/-q/-n/-h/--` + positionals, `is_uint`, `need_value`, KEEP validation) and `resolve_dir`, with the same double-sourcing guard style as `lib/log.sh`. `rotate.sh` and `verify.sh` source it (after defining `usage`/`parse_local_option`, as the parser runs at source time) and accept exactly the same flags/exit codes — verified against 11 flag/error cases. `backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `report.sh` untouched.

**Tests** (`tests/run_tests.sh`): one test per bug — rotate with 3 archives and `--keep 3` deletes nothing (fails on the old code, which deleted the newest); verify of `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz` reports ok / rc=0. `bash tests/run_tests.sh`: 8/8 ok.

Changed files: rotate.sh, verify.sh, tests/run_tests.sh, and new lib/common.sh.
